title: Chelsea Soccer Club Has a New Boss — And a Big Goal
summary:
Have you ever played a game where the team gets new owners? That just happened to Chelsea, one of the biggest soccer clubs in England. On Wednesday, Chelsea announced that a company called Clearlake Capital would buy the shares of Todd Boehly and Mark Walter. That means Clearlake now controls the club.

Boehly and Walter are American billionaires. They bought Chelsea in May 2022 with Clearlake after the British government forced a sale by the previous owner, Roman Abramovich. Before this new deal, Clearlake already owned 61.5 percent. Now it owns even more. The Financial Times says Boehly and Walter will get 950 million pounds (about $1.27 billion) for their shares. The whole club is worth about 5 billion pounds.

So what does this mean for the team? Chelsea's coach, Xabi Alonso, spoke to reporters on Thursday. "Our ambition is clear: to compete at the highest level, to win major trophies, and to build sustained success," the club said. Alonso started as coach on July 1. He said he has a good relationship with Behdad Eghbali, one of Clearlake's leaders. "He was the one that came to Madrid to explain to me the project," Alonso said.

Chelsea hasn't been winning everything lately. Last season, the team finished 10th in the Premier League — not great for a club this big. This season, they have seven points from four games and sit sixth. Alonso's job is to turn things around. Will the new owners help? Fans will be watching.
why_it_matters: Big sports teams are also businesses, so when owners change, it can affect ticket prices, which players join the team, and how the club that kids grow up watching performs in the years ahead.

background_read: Chelsea (a famous soccer club based in London, England) plays in the Premier League, the top men's soccer league in England, which has 20 teams.
The club has been owned by many different people over the years, including the Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich (a very rich businessman), who was forced to sell Chelsea in 2022.
Clearlake Capital (an investment company that puts money into businesses) bought the club back then together with Todd Boehly and Mark Walter, and it has now taken even more control.

perspectives.description: Fans may hope the new owners spend money on great players, because the club says it wants to win major trophies.
Some fans worry that when clubs are bought and sold like companies, tickets get more expensive and the team's traditions matter less than profit.
Ownership changes are normal for huge soccer clubs; Chelsea itself has changed hands several times, and the team still has to win games on the field.
